Hi all — quick legal read and suggested edits below. I attached a clean markup (ExhibitF_karthik_comments.pdf) with inline notes, but summary first:

1) TERM: Atlas requested a 12-month extension. We can accept a 12-month term but we need to preserve the existing auto-renewal language in Section 2. Proposed compromise: accept 12-month fixed term for this amendment, with original MSA auto-renew still in effect thereafter. (Suggest redline included in attached PDF.)

2) DATA RETENTION (Exhibit F §4): Atlas requests 18 months. Our standard is 12 months for logs; 18 months increases support exposure. Proposed language: Redwood will retain logs for 12 months; Redwood is willing to retain troubleshooting logs for up to 18 months on mutually agreed escalation requests (documented by ticket). This gives Atlas more time without changing our baseline retention.

3) SLAs & BURSTING: The order form requests a 40% peak buffer. Ops/engineering needs to confirm how burst-to-dedicated routing will behave. If we can't guarantee hard reservable burst, we should add an explicit fallback clause: "If reserved capacity is insufficient, requests will be routed to compatible hosted capacity with best-effort latency and documented rate limit behavior."

4) LIMITATION OF LIABILITY: I noted Atlas's redline expands exclusions — we should push back. Keeping that narrow will be my ask.

I recommend a fast touch-base with Atlas legal on Friday to resolve the data-retention language and the burst fallback. If Atlas insists on a 18-month baseline retention, escalate to product/security for a risk review.

Attachments referenced: ExhibitF_karthik_comments.pdf (PDF, ~6 pages)

Tom / Sarah — quick operational summary and proposed path to signature.

1) Capacity: We can support the +40% peak buffer as requested. Practically, that will be handled via temporary reserved headroom from our Dedicated pool plus auto-burst into compatible hosted capacity. We will document the routing priority and expected latency ranges in an appendix to the order form (draft attached).

2) Term: Redwood can accept a 24-month firm term only if Atlas agrees to a modest ramp payment schedule (50% of incremental for Q1 then remaining 50% across next two quarters) to cover reservation costs. If procurement is ok with that timing, we can include a short payment schedule table in the order form.

3) Retention: We are prepared to commit to an 18-month troubleshooting log retention for tickets opened within the retention window; we cannot unilaterally change the baseline global retention policy. We will add explicit ticketing/resolution SLAs tied to retention access in Exhibit F.

Next steps:
